text: What is the primary advantage of using photons rather than electrons as information carriers for computing?
choices: Photons have higher rest mass, enabling more stable storage
Photons travel at the speed of light and do not generate resistive heat losses
Photonic circuits can be miniaturised below 1 nm, surpassing electronic lithography limits
Photons naturally perform Boolean logic without additional components
explanation: The key advantage of photonics for computing is that photons travel at the speed of light in the medium and do not experience resistive (Ohmic) energy dissipation — the dominant energy bottleneck in electronics. Photons also allow wavelength-division multiplexing (many channels on one waveguide) and are immune to electromagnetic interference. The miniaturisation limit for photonics is set by the diffraction limit (~wavelength/2), not by lithography, so electronics still wins at raw density.
